name: Toy ruleset
description: The fast unit-test ruleset. Its constants are the original's confirmed values, transcribed from the reports in the research repository's docs/reports/ and cited per field in the sibling "_provenance" blocks; its flags are set the way the shipped classical-faithful preset sets them. It exists so tests do not depend on the full classical-mediterranean world, which task T29 exports separately.

_provenance.weekStep: confirmed: decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md — the week advances by +2 each turn cycle.
_provenance.seasonAdvanceFromWeek: confirmed: decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md — the season advances at the 11 to 1 wrap.
_provenance.seasonsPerYear: confirmed: decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md — 'quarterly' is once per season, four times a year; the year decrements at the Winter to Spring wrap.
_provenance.startWeek: confirmed: impconq2-full-save-analysis.md and one-turn-save-comparison.md — the earliest news slot in the sample saves reads 'Week 1      Spring      270 BC', and the next turn's slot reads 'Week  3      Spring      270BC'. The parity is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md gives the cycle as 'week = (week + 2) mod 12; if week == 1: season++', so only an odd start ever reaches the season boundary. Every dated save in the project (weeks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 — saves-and-screenshots.md, strategic-recording-and-summer-saves.md) is on that odd parity.
_provenance.startSeasonIndex: confirmed: saves-and-screenshots.md and strategic-recording-and-summer-saves.md — the save trailer's +44 byte is 0 in all five Spring saves and 1 in all three Summer saves, so season index 0 is Spring; impconq2-full-save-analysis.md shows the campaign's first dated news slot as Spring 270 BC.
_provenance.startYearBc: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — THumanFalls_InitializeForm reports the reign length as 270 minus the current year, confirming the 270 BC start.
_provenance.cityUnitStateCodeStep: confirmed: decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md — city-unit StateCode increments by 2 per week.
_provenance.cityUnitStateCodeCap: confirmed: decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md — capped at 24 (a cap, not a starting value).

_provenance.recruitCost: confirmed: unit-type-stat-table-in-dat.md — +0x22, the initial recruit cost.
_provenance.quarterlyPrice: confirmed: unit-type-stat-table-in-dat.md — +0x24, the quarterly price used by upkeep and mercenary hire.
_provenance.combatPowerWeight: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — +0x26, identified there as the per-type combat-power weight used by field-battle strength.

_provenance.shots: confirmed: unit-type-stat-table-in-dat.md — matches the '1st Lancers Battalion ... 9 shots' screenshot in battle-observation.md.
_provenance.recruitCost: confirmed: unit-type-stat-table-in-dat.md — independently solved from two save-diffs in decompiled-recruitment-cost-formula.md before the table was found.

_provenance.moveCosts: confirmed: terrain-move-cost-table-in-dat.md — the original's twelve-entry terrain table at DAT offset 0x1F622, verbatim: Sea 1, Sea 3, Plain 1, Desert 1, Forest 2, Mountains 4, and six River codes at 4. The table is keyed by tile-type id rather than by cell code so that a world with different or additional terrain types can be priced by the same ruleset shape; the twelve entries are shipped values, not a fixed size.
_provenance.defaultMoveCost: designed: docs/game-design.md §Movement — 'A custom World's new terrain types default to cost 1 unless a ruleset explicitly prices them'. Searched docs/reports/ for any original handling of an unpriced terrain code and found none to transcribe: terrain-move-cost-table-in-dat.md establishes that the original's table covers exactly codes 0-11 and that codes 12 and above are city/army/fleet markers rather than terrain, so the original has no unpriced-terrain case to copy.

_provenance.consumptionBaseValue: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md, citing decompiled-turn-and-calendar-sequencing.md's FUN_004514ec — per-turn consumption = ((90 - seasonVal) * troops) / 20000, decompiled directly and verified turn-for-turn against the Thracian army's spring consumption (142 -> 98 -> 54 -> 10, exactly -44 each turn).
_provenance.consumptionDivisor: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the 20000 divisor of the same expression.
_provenance.fleetEmbarkedDivisor: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — an army aboard a fleet (army[+8] == -1) instead consumes max(0, supplies - troops/200), no seasonal term.
_provenance.seasonValues: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the season record at DAT offset 0x1F7D8, matching &DAT_004794a8 + season*10: Spring 50, Summer 80, Autumn 80, Winter 20, indexed by calendar.startSeasonIndex's convention (0=Spring). Winter costs 7x Summer, verified against the same investigation's seasonal-consumption table for a 22,000-troop army (44/11/11/77 tons).

_provenance.decayThresholdPercent: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md, FUN_004514ec — pct < 10 decays morale by 2 and costs one move; verified turn-for-turn against the Thracian army's 13-save series (12 of 12 transitions predicted exactly).
_provenance.deadBandUpperPercent: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — 10 <= pct <= 15 is a deliberate dead band, no change.
_provenance.moraleFloor: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the real bound of the field: the army panel prints morale as a tier via moraleNames[(v-51)>>2], 51...70 being exactly five 4-wide tiers.
_provenance.regenAmount: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — army[+14] += 1 when pct > 15, the confirmed 2:1 decay/regen asymmetry (decay is twice as fast as regen).
_provenance.moraleCeiling: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the real ceiling of the field.
_provenance.movesPenaltyOnDecay: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — army[+6] -= 1 on the same pct < 10 branch that decays morale; verified against the Thracian series' moves column (9 while supplied, 8 from the first pct < 10 turn on).
_provenance.baseMovesMax: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md, FUN_004514ec — moves = 10 - min(5, troops / 20000), recomputed every turn before the decay penalty, not accumulated from the previous turn.
_provenance.movesTroopDivisor: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the troop divisor of the same base-moves expression; numerically the same 20000 as supplyConsumption.consumptionDivisor in the source pseudocode, kept as a separate field since the two formulas are conceptually distinct.
_provenance.movesReductionCap: confirmed: investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md — the min(5, ...) cap of the same expression.

effects.description: A storm damages a fleet at sea.

_provenance._group: designed: docs/game-design.md §Economy — 'implement as a data-driven table of possible weather effects (storm damages a fleet, drought reduces a region's supply, etc.) with the confirmed frequency curve and [designed] specific effects'. decompiled-weather-events.md confirms the frequency curve only; FUN_004511bc (the effect itself) was never decompiled, so no magnitude is transcribed here — this entry names the effect kind design-audit.md already suggests, nothing more.

effects.description: A drought reduces a region's supply.

_provenance._group: designed: docs/game-design.md §Economy, same open item as storm-damages-fleet — no magnitude transcribed, effect internals unrecovered.

_provenance.earlyLateWeekThreshold: confirmed: decompiled-weather-events.md — Spring and Autumn each have a distinct 'early' (week < 6) and 'late' (week >= 6) odds band; Summer and Winter are flat for the whole season.
_provenance.bySeason: confirmed: decompiled-weather-events.md — Spring early 1-in-15 / late 1-in-30; Summer 1-in-40; Autumn early 1-in-30 / late 1-in-15; Winter 1-in-5. Winter is roughly 8x more frequent than Summer (1/5 vs 1/40), the source for T08's DoD 8 ratio-band assertion, itself approximate per that report.
_provenance.effects: designed: docs/game-design.md §Economy — the frequency curve is confirmed but the effects were never decompiled (FUN_004511bc, [open] per docs/design-audit.md §2.13); this table exists so an effect can be added as data later without an engine change, not because these two entries' specifics are evidenced.

_provenance.shipUpkeepPerQuarter: confirmed: fleet-order-at-caere.md and decompiled-fleet-tax-and-mercenary-formulas.md — ships cost 3 talents each per quarter.
_provenance.unityCap: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — the instant resolver clamps the winner's unity with min(990, ...).
_provenance.purseCapPerUnit: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TAFSupply_ChangeMoney caps an army's or fleet's own purse at 1,000 talents.
_provenance.supplyTonsPerTalent: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TAFSupply_TransferSupply charges amount / 5, i.e. 1 talent per 5 tons, from the buyer's purse to the selling city's owner. docs/design-audit.md Q9 is now answered by the user's own play experience: resupplying at a city the buying army's nation owns is free (no talent debit at all, matching the Galatia frames' unchanged army money and treasury); this amount/5 constant applies only to the paid, foreign-city case. Where a foreign purchase's talents end up (the selling city owner's treasury, or nowhere) is still [open] — Ruleset.Economy has no field for a credit destination, deliberately: SupplyPurchase debits only and invents no destination.
_provenance.armySupplyTonsPerTroops: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — army supply capacity is troops / 100 tons, reproducing all four recorded percentage readings.
_provenance.fleetSupplyTonsPerShip: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — fleet supply capacity is ships × 8 tons.
_provenance.supplyPercentNumerator: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TInformation_ShowArmyDetails prints the supply percentage as supplies × 10000 / troops.
_provenance.unpaidUpkeepTroopLossDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md — army units lose troops, reduced by troops/100, when available upkeep funds drop below 1. A real consequence, not a debt counter.
_provenance.lowTaxLoyaltyThresholdPercent: confirmed: decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md — if a nation's tax rate is under 11% and a city's loyalty is below 80, there's a chance loyalty rises.
_provenance.lowTaxLoyaltyCityThreshold: confirmed: decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md — the city-loyalty side of the same condition.
_provenance.rebellionLoyaltyThreshold: derived: decompiled-quarterly-billing-and-economy.md — 'cities with loyalty under 30 can trigger it'; the rebellion check itself (FUN_0044c204) was never decompiled, so this is the confirmed structure's threshold, not the exact check. docs/design-audit.md §2 calls this out explicitly as needing a placeholder tagged accordingly; see EconomyRules.RebellionLoyaltyThreshold's own doc comment.

_provenance.troopsPerCostUnit: confirmed: decompiled-recruitment-cost-formula.md — cost = (troops / 200) × priceTable[unitType], the same table for initial recruitment and quarterly upkeep.
_provenance.mercenaryPoolSlots: confirmed: decompiled-sav-file-layout.md — the mercenary table is exactly 50 slots of 12 bytes, hard-coded in the save/load code (mercenary-pool-record.md had found the same figure empirically).
_provenance.mercenaryHireTroopDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — hire cost = (troops × quarterlyPrice[type]) / 1000 × quality, paid from the hiring army's own purse.
_provenance.mercenaryUpkeepQualityDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — mercenary upkeep is ((troops / 200) × price[type] × quality) / 5 against a regular's (troops / 200) × price[type].

_provenance.maxUnitsPerArmy: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TUnitMap_JoinArmies caps the combined army at 20 units.
_provenance.maxTroopsPerArmy: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — and the same 100,000 cap is enforced on mercenary hire.
_provenance.maxArmies: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — FUN_00449F08 refuses to create an army once 198 exist (< 0xC6).
_provenance.splitMinUnits: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TUnitMap_SplitArmy needs at least 2 units.
_provenance.newArmyMorale: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — a freshly split army is created with morale 0x3B = 59.
_provenance.newArmyMovesHumanSeat: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — 0 moves for a human nation.
_provenance.newArmyMovesAiSeat: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — 1 move for an AI one. This is one of the seat asymmetries the flags block selects between.

_provenance.buildCostPerShip: confirmed: fleet-order-at-caere.md and decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — a fleet order costs ships × 10 talents.
_provenance.orderMinShips: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TBuildFleet_ChangeFleetSize clamps an order to 10..100 ships.
_provenance.constructionTicks: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — the construction counter starts at 24 and decrements weekly; the Caere order's 12-ticks-to-go reading twelve weeks later confirms it in save data.
_provenance.launchConditionPercent: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — FUN_0044A050 sets fleet +20 to 100 on launch.
_provenance.transportTroopsPerShip: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — the embark check refuses when ships < troops / 500.
_provenance.repairCostDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — repair costs ships × points / 5 talents and zeroes the fleet's moves.
_provenance.joinMaxShips: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TUnitMap_JoinFleets refuses a combined fleet above 100 ships.
_provenance.splitMinShips: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TUnitMap_SplitFleet needs at least 20 ships.
_provenance.maxConditionPercent: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — TRepairFleet clamps a repair order to 0..(100 - condition).

_provenance.unitySwingShipDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — a naval battle moves unity by plus or minus floor(loserShips / 2), not by the field battle's flat 25.
_provenance.carriedArmyPowerDivisor: confirmed [T31 correction]: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md describes this as 'a carried army adds armyPower / 50', but FUN_0044AA54 (naval battle resolution) calls FUN_0044A930 -- siege strength, not FUN_0044A8CC's armyPower -- so a carried army adds siege strength / 50. Found reading FUN_0044A98C/FUN_0044A930 while decompiling siege defender strength; see docs/investigations/siege-defender-strength.md. Value unchanged at 50.
_provenance.randomBandCount: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — random(4) picks one of four bands.
_provenance.randomBandPercent: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — each band is 10% of the base, giving a 0/10/20/30% bonus.
_provenance.winnerDamageDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — FUN_0044B4F8 costs the winner ships × d / 300 and condition × d / 300.
_provenance.damageRatioScale: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — r = max(1, loserStrength × 100 / winnerStrength) and d = r squared / 100.
_provenance.unitLossDamageThreshold: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — above d = 70 a carried army also loses whole units.
_provenance.unitLossDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — unitCount × d / 250 units are lost at random.

_provenance.survivorCasualtyNumerator: designed: docs/game-design.md §'The defeated side's fate' — the improved ruleset mirrors the winner's own confirmed casualty ratio onto the loser instead of destroying it. Searched docs/reports/ for any partial-defeat or retreat outcome in the original and found none: all three decompiled resolvers (decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md) annihilate the loser unconditionally, so there is no original number to transcribe. Default chosen to equal the winner's cap so only one number needs retuning.
_provenance.scatterTilesMin: designed: docs/game-design.md §'The defeated side's fate' — survivors relocate 2 to 4 tiles from the battle site. Same search as above: the original has no relocation-on-defeat behaviour to measure, so this is a documented placeholder meant to be retuned from play.
_provenance.scatterTilesMax: designed: docs/game-design.md §'The defeated side's fate'. Same search and same status as scatterTilesMin.

_provenance.meleeLossCapPercent: confirmed: battle-recording-melee-cap-confirmed.md — the melee loss cap is floor(0.4 × defenderTroops) + 1, matching four of five recorded exchanges exactly and the fifth being below the cap.
_provenance.meleeLossCapOffset: confirmed: battle-recording-melee-cap-confirmed.md — the '+ 1' of the same expression.
_provenance.meleeLossHardCap: confirmed: decompiled-combat-formula-structure.md — melee losses are additionally capped at 30,000.
_provenance.meleeBasePowerFloor: confirmed: combat-type-effectiveness-matrix.md, quoting decompiled-combat-formula-structure.md — the melee power term ends '+ 12', so a zero-effectiveness matchup still deals minimum damage.
_provenance.inRangeShotMultiplier: confirmed: decompiled-combat-formula-structure.md — shots that are in range are doubled.
_provenance.typeEffectiveness: confirmed values, candidate orientation: combat-type-effectiveness-matrix.md — the 25 values are read directly from the DAT file immediately after the unit-type table, but that report is explicit that the attacker-row versus defender-row assignment is a reasoned inference, not re-traced index arithmetic. Rows are read here as the attacker, matching the report's chosen orientation; typeEffectivenessOrder records which axis order the rows and columns use so a later correction is a data change.
_provenance._group: This whole block belongs to the optional 'detailed' resolver held in reserve by docs/game-design.md §Combat. The shipped instant resolver does not read any of it; it is carried here so that adding the reserve resolver later is a ruleset change rather than a model change.

_provenance.powerTroopDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — field-battle strength is (sum of powerWeight[type] × troops / 100) / 80 × morale.
_provenance.powerDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — the / 80 of the same expression, shared by both army-strength functions.
_provenance.winnerCasualtyNumerator: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — the winner takes loserPower × 40 / winnerPower casualties.
_provenance.absorbedSupplyTroopDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — absorbed supplies are capped at winnerTroops / 100, the same capacity rule as buying supply.
_provenance.qualityFloor: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — every surviving unit is raised to at least quality 6 ('average').
_provenance.qualityCap: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — the further promotion is clamped at 9 ('elite').
_provenance.unitySwing: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — the loser's nation loses 25 unity and the winner's gains 25.
_provenance.autoPeaceChanceNumerator: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — random(5) < 2, a 2-in-5 chance of an automatic peace treaty after a decisive AI-versus-AI field battle.
_provenance.autoPeaceLoserUnityThreshold: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — gated on the loser's unity above 500.
_provenance.autoPeaceLoserCityThreshold: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — and on the loser holding more than 7 cities.

_provenance.archerStrengthMultiplier: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — siege strength is (sum of troops, archers counted three times) / 80 × morale; also stated in decompiled-city-capture-resolution.md.
_provenance.powerDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — the / 80 of the same expression.
_provenance.defenderFortificationWeight: confirmed [T31, superseding T02]: FUN_0044A98C itself (decompiled directly, not read off decompiled-city-capture-resolution.md, which is the source of T02's error) computes defender strength as loyalty × 150 + finishedFortificationPercent × 250 + populationThousands × 200. T02 had swapped this weight and defenderLoyaltyWeight's, attaching 150 to fortification and 250 to loyalty; corrected here. Field identity independently confirmed by TInformation_ShowCityDetails (0x0043BE5C), whose 'Fortification -' label reads the same DAT_004795aa word with the identical '< 0x65' guard FortificationCode.FinishedPercent already implements. See docs/investigations/siege-defender-strength.md.
_provenance.defenderLoyaltyWeight: confirmed [T31, superseding T02]: the loyalty × 150 term of FUN_0044A98C, decompiled directly. T02 had this at 250 (swapped with defenderFortificationWeight); corrected here. TInformation_ShowCityDetails's 'Loyalty -' label reads the same DAT_004795a6 word, dividing by 10 for its tier string — the same tiering LoyaltyRules.TierDivisor already ships. See docs/investigations/siege-defender-strength.md.
_provenance.defenderPopulationWeight: confirmed [T31, superseding T02]: FUN_0044A98C's third defender-strength term reads DAT_004795ac (population, in thousands) × 200. decompiled-city-capture-resolution.md, which T02's shipped defenderUnidentifiedFieldWeight was transcribed from, recorded the weight but never named the field because it had not decompiled this function. TInformation_ShowCityDetails's 'Population -' label (0x0043BE5C) prints the same DAT_004795ac × 1000, confirming the identity independently of the weight's magnitude. Weight unchanged at 200. See docs/investigations/siege-defender-strength.md.
_provenance.highFortificationThreshold: confirmed: decompiled-city-capture-resolution.md — 'if <condition> and fortification > 59: strength = strength × 5 / 3'. The report is explicit that the branch carries a further condition it did not recover, so the threshold is confirmed but the branch's full guard is not. T31's decompilation of FUN_0044A98C identifies that condition as FUN_0044B8D0 (whether the city is its controlling nation's capital) and the branch as gated on loyalty > 59, not fortification > 59 -- both misnamings are real but are filed as issue #46 rather than fixed in this task (see build-orchestration-plan.md T31's 'Bugs logged, not fixed here').
_provenance.highFortificationBonusNumerator: confirmed: decompiled-city-capture-resolution.md — the × 5 / 3 of the same branch. See highFortificationThreshold for the unrecovered guard.
_provenance.highFortificationBonusDenominator: confirmed: decompiled-city-capture-resolution.md — the / 3 of the same branch.
_provenance.defenderGarrisonTroopDivisor: confirmed: decompiled-city-capture-resolution.md — 'strength += (garrison troops assigned to this city) / 2'.
_provenance.defenderOwnerNotAllegiancePenaltyPercent: confirmed as read, but UNRECONCILED: decompiled-city-capture-resolution.md describes a 20% defender penalty when the city's owner is not its allegiance. docs/design-audit.md §2.13 flags that the siege entry point FUN_0044B27C instead applies a 10% reduction when the ATTACKING nation equals the city's allegiance, and that FUN_0044A98C (defender strength) was never decompiled, so the two readings may be one adjustment or two. Both are carried here as separate fields, unresolved, rather than one being silently dropped. This is an evidence conflict for whoever implements siege resolution (task T17) to settle, not for this task to pick.
_provenance.attackerIsAllegianceDefenderReductionPer: confirmed as read, but UNRECONCILED: see the note on defenderOwnerNotAllegiancePenaltyPercent. Source: docs/design-audit.md §2.13 reporting FUN_0044B27C's ×9/10 branch.

_provenance.defectionFloor: confirmed: decompiled-defection-and-siege-attrition.md — a defection pulls loyalty toward 65 and changes neither population nor fortification.
_provenance.allegiantRecaptureTarget: confirmed: galatia-elimination-and-city-resupply-confirmed.md — loyalty moves toward 90 when the allegiant nation recaptures its own city.

_provenance.cooldownAfterBrokenAlliance: confirmed: decompiled-diplomacy-peace-terms-and-instant-battles.md — -24 when an alliance is broken.

_provenance.cityPopulationTierThresholds: OMITTED (ships empty) — and here is exactly what was searched and exactly what was found, because an earlier revision of this note claimed the search came up empty when it had not. What the reports DO establish: rivers-and-map-markers.md ('City and unit overlays') finds that all 334 city cells satisfy 'map code = 20 + owner code + 16 × variant' with variants 0-4, holding for 334/334 cities in the checked save — so a five-value display axis on city markers is well evidenced, the direct counterpart of the three army bands and three fleet bands in decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md part 3. What the reports do NOT establish: that same sentence says the variant's meaning — 'city size, icon, or another display category' — still needs confirmation, and the report's own next-check item 3 is 'confirm the city-marker variant meanings'. There is no decompiled banding function for cities analogous to FUN_0044A80C/FUN_0044A878, so no population boundary is recorded anywhere. Shipping 5 as a size-tier count would assert the unconfirmed half (that the variant means size); shipping any threshold would invent a number outright. So this ships empty and docs/game-design.md §'City and army markers scale with size' is left standing as a requirement rather than a spec. Closing it needs that report's next-check item 3, after which the thresholds arrive as data with no model change.
